## Legs: run vs queued

### Engineering legs — RAN (offline only)

- `data/procurement_vocab.toml` — `[platform_endpoints.legistar]` gains
  `keyword_index_query` (`$filter=({or_group})&$top=1000&$skip={skip}`),
  `keyword_index_page_size = 1000`, `keyword_index_max_pages = 25`,
  `keyword_index_groups` — the I8 §4.1 term set verbatim (38 terms) in
  four OR-groups; every generated URL measures ~430–550 chars (bound
  ~1,500). The recency `index_query` is byte-identical;
  `doc_per_tenant = 20` / `doc_run_cap = 350` / `doc_order_fields`
  unchanged.
- `procurement.py` — `tenant_targets()` emits the recency target plus
  one `paged` keyword target per OR-group (`<tenant>:kw{0..3}`) carrying
  the filled query template, terms, page bounds, corrected jurisdiction
  and doc caps as data. `fetch()` routes `paged` targets through
  `_fetch_paged_index`: pages `$skip` by `page_size` through the shared
  fetcher until a short page or `max_pages` (recorded `truncated` on the
  merged capture's `sig_paged` provenance); a first-page non-200/error
  envelope/non-JSON flows through unmerged; a mid-slice failure keeps
  the fetched pages and marks the slice truncated. `extract()` applies
  `_agenda_precise_items` to keyword slices only — a title survives only
  on a `agenda_content_vocab.toml` match (word-boundary, case-insensitive
  — the I4 Q5 collation inference, fixture-pinned by the ALL-CAPS cabq
  title) — and emits an `agenda_index_slice` outcome row per paged slice
  (pages, `items_count`, `precise_count`, `dropped_count`). The recency
  slice stays unfiltered; a matter seen by both passes is one claim
  through `content_digest`. `discover_more()` groups index captures by
  `tenant_id` and dedupes items by item id BEFORE bounded selection —
  the reviewed per-tenant window bounds the merged item set, never a
  per-capture window (the second pass cannot double document fan-out).
  `discover()` dedupes agenda targets on id + URL (was `tenant_id`) so a
  supplied recency row never suppresses the generated keyword slices.
  `normalize()` stamps `agenda_index_slice` as run-record data
  (usaspending/ted slice precedent), never a claim.
- `data/agenda_content_vocab.toml` — `vocab_version` → `2026.10.10`,
  additions only: `automated_traffic_enforcement`, `mobile_forensics`,
  `video_analytics`, `biometric`, `electronic_monitoring`,
  `school_surveillance` term rows plus vendor rows the keyword terms
  name (`axon`, `briefcam`, `genetec`, `rekor`, `fusus`,
  `verra_mobility`, `clearview_ai` — disambiguated forms only, the CROL
  false-positive class); `alpr` gains `license plate`/`licence plate`/
  `license plate camera`; `drone` gains `unmanned aero`;
  `gunshot_detection` gains `gunshot locat`/`gunfire locat`;
  `social_media_monitoring` gains the SMM vendor names on word
  boundaries (I4 NEW-6 — bare substrings are how `Brinc` lands inside
  `Parsons Brinckerhoff`). No prior row or pattern rewritten; forbidden
  tokens and person-naming predicates unchanged.
- Tenant verification (deliverable 5) — `ousd` and `washoe_county_nv`
  confirmed genuine InSite tenants (`platform = "legistar"`,
  `api_base = "https://webapi.legistar.com/v1/…"`): the widened pass

- `task_timeout` (deliverable 6) — the legistar cadence row already

- Tests + fixtures — `tests/connectors/test_agenda_keyword_pass.py`

## Deviations

- Paging lands in `fetch()` (one bounded loop per keyword target,
  pages merged into ONE capture with `sig_paged` provenance) rather
  than emitting page targets through discovery — the pipeline's
  continuation seam is the single-pass document fan-out (`P26.6`), and
  page targets there could not know a page count ahead of fetch. Every
  page still goes through the shared `ctx.fetcher`; the merged capture
  records every page URL + count, and the bound (`max_pages`) is a
  recorded truncation, never a silent stop. Recorded, not a scope
  expansion.
- `task_timeout = "3h"` was already staged on the legistar cadence row
  by P35.6's per-row mechanism — deliverable 6 is verified by test
  (`ops/cadence.toml` untouched in this row), not raised.
- The `keyword_index_groups` term set carries `body-worn`/`body worn`
  (deliverable 2's monitoring/BWC class) — server-side broad; the
  client-side `body.?worn` pattern keeps the true hits and the
  vocabulary bump adds the EM/school/ATE/forensics/analytics classes the
  filter needs to keep the §4.1 hits.
- No new ADR — the row executes the ticket contract; the
  fetch-time paging shape is recorded here as the deviation note, not a
  contract change.
